name: David Zwirner
description: A monolithic blue-chip gallery in Chelsea known for staging blockbuster installations,  including frequent Yayoi Kusama infinity rooms.

name: Pace Gallery
description: An eight-story mega-gallery dominating the Chelsea art district. The scale of the  exhibitions rivals major global museums.

name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
description: The twin reflecting pools are powerful even before you go inside. The museum is emotionally intense — plan 2-3 hours. 25th anniversary in September 2026.
must_try: Museum audio guide + memorial pools at dusk

name: Edge at Hudson Yards
description: Outdoor sky deck with a glass floor 1,100 feet up. The highest outdoor observation deck in the Western Hemisphere. Not for the faint of heart.
must_try: City Climb (outdoor climbing experience on the building's exterior)

name: One World Observatory
description: 102 floors up in 47 seconds. The SkyPod elevator ride is an experience by itself. Views span all five boroughs and three states.
must_try: Go at sunset for both daylight and city lights views

name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
description: Book the crown access months in advance. Ellis Island immigration museum is the sleeper hit — most people rush through it. Ferry from Battery Park or Liberty State Park NJ.
must_try: Crown access (book 3+ months ahead) + Ellis Island immigration records lookup

name: Top of the Rock Observation Deck
description: Better than the Empire State Building because you can SEE the Empire State Building. Three levels, open-air top deck, Central Park to the north, downtown to the south.
must_try: Sunset timing for golden hour over the skyline

name: American Museum of Natural History
address: 200 Central Park West, Upper West Side, Manhattan
description: The dinosaurs, the planetarium, the blue whale — you saw it in Night at the Museum and it's even better in person. The new Gilder Center wing is stunning.
must_try: Fossil Halls + Hayden Planetarium space show

name: Brooklyn Museum
description: Massive, progressive, and far less crowded than its Manhattan rivals. Their First  Saturdays program is legendary in Brooklyn.
must_try: The Dinner Party by Judy Chicago

name: Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum
address: 2 E 91st St, Upper East Side, Manhattan
description: Housed in Andrew Carnegie's former mansion, this is the nation's only museum  dedicated to historic and contemporary design.
must_try: The interactive pen provided upon entry

name: MoMA PS1
address: 22-25 Jackson Ave, Long Island City, Queens
description: MoMA's contemporary art outpost in a converted school building in Queens. Free admission all of 2026 for its 50th anniversary. Edgier and less crowded than the mothership.
must_try: Whatever the current installation is — they rotate constantly

name: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)
description: Starry Night, Campbell's Soup Cans, Monet's Water Lilies — all here. The sculpture garden is a free oasis in Midtown. Free Friday evenings.

name: Museum of the City of New York
description: Often overlooked by tourists, this is the definitive archive of NYC's evolution. The  ongoing 'New York at Its Core' exhibit is mandatory viewing.
must_try: New York at Its Core exhibition

name: Neue Galerie
description: A gilded mansion dedicated exclusively to early 20th-century German and Austrian art.  Home to Klimt's famed 'Woman in Gold'.
must_try: Gustav Klimt's Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I

name: New Museum
description: A stack of asymmetrical silver boxes housing aggressive, boundary-pushing  contemporary art. Not for traditionalists.
must_try: The panoramic view from the Sky Room

name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
description: Frank Lloyd Wright's spiral. Walk the ramp. The building IS the art. Whatever exhibition is on is secondary to the architecture.
must_try: Walk the full spiral top to bottom

name: Tenement Museum
address: 103 Orchard St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: Guided tours through meticulously restored immigrant apartments. An intensely  emotional and vital look into the working-class history of New York.
must_try: Hard Times or Sweatshop Workers Tour

name: The Met Cloisters
address: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, Fort Tryon Park, Manhattan
description: A stunning reconstruction of European medieval abbeys perched on a hill overlooking  the Hudson River. Feels entirely detached from NYC.

name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
description: 2 million works spanning 5,000 years. You could come every day for a year and not see it all. The rooftop garden in summer has the best view in Manhattan.
must_try: Egyptian Temple of Dendur, then the rooftop bar in summer

name: Whitney Museum of American Art
description: American art from the 20th century forward in Renzo Piano's Meatpacking building. The terraces overlooking the Hudson are worth the admission alone.
must_try: Outdoor terraces on every floor + Whitney Biennial years
hours: Mon, Wed, Thu, Sun 10:30am-6pm; Fri-Sat 10:30am-10pm; closed Tue

name: Broadway (Theater District)
address: Times Square area, W 41st-54th St between 6th-8th Ave, Manhattan
description: 41 professional theaters. The Lion King, Hamilton, Wicked, whatever is new — there's a reason this is the global capital of live theater. TKTS booth in Times Square for same-day discounted tickets.
must_try: TKTS booth for 20-50% off same-day tickets

name: Circle Line Sightseeing Cruises
address: Pier 83, W 42nd St, Midtown West, Manhattan
description: The quintessential tourist boat. The 'Best of NYC' cruise circumnavigates the entire  island, offering unbeatable skyline views.

name: Manhattan by Sail
description: Ditch the ferry fumes for a historic schooner. Sailing past the Statue of Liberty at sunset  with a cocktail is pure magic.
must_try: Sunset Sail on the Clipper City

name: Scott's Pizza Tours
description: An obsessive, nerdy, and deeply delicious deep dive into the thermal dynamics and  history of NYC pizza. Highly educational.

name: Brooklyn Brewery
description: The flagship that helped put craft beer on the map in Brooklyn. Taproom with rotating drafts. Free tours on weekends.

name: House of Yes
description: Bushwick performance venue / nightclub / circus. Themed parties, aerial performers, consent culture front and center. Dress up or don't bother.

name: Bemelmans Bar
address: 35 E 76th St (The Carlyle Hotel), Upper East Side, Manhattan
description: Old-money cocktail bar inside The Carlyle with original Ludwig Bemelmans murals on the walls. Live jazz, $30 martinis, and the most glamorous room in the city.
must_try: Classic martini while the jazz trio plays

name: Dead Rabbit
description: Multi-floor cocktail bar consistently ranked among the world's best. Irish pub downstairs, cocktail parlor upstairs. The menu reads like a novel.
must_try: Any cocktail from the parlor menu (they rotate seasonally)

name: Please Don't Tell (PDT)
address: 113 St Marks Pl, East Village, Manhattan
description: Enter through a phone booth inside Crif Dogs hot dog shop. The OG speakeasy revival bar. Reservations at 3pm sharp, gone in seconds.
must_try: Mezcal Mule (or whatever seasonal cocktail catches your eye)

name: McSorley's Old Ale House
description: NYC's oldest bar, open since 1854. Two choices: light or dark ale. Cash only. Sawdust on the floor. Lincoln drank here. So should you.
must_try: Two mugs of dark ale (they always come in pairs)

name: King Cole Bar
description: A staggeringly expensive, opulent hotel bar boasting a Maxfield Parrish mural. It claims  to have invented the Bloody Mary.

name: Lobby Bar at The Bowery Hotel
description: Oozing atmosphere with crimson velvet, antique sofas, and a roaring fireplace. Excellent  people-watching for downtown's fashion elite.

name: The Campbell
description: Hidden inside Grand Central, this former tycoon's office feels like stepping into the  1920s. Dress well, as the ambiance demands it.

name: Cubbyhole
description: A legendary, chaotic, and deeply lovable lesbian bar. The ceiling is covered in paper  lanterns and the jukebox is always blasting.

name: Henrietta Hudson
description: A core anchor for queer women-centered nightlife since 1991. Expect strong drinks, a  packed dance floor, and a devoted community.

name: Julius'
description: The oldest gay bar in NYC, predating Stonewall. Unpretentious, affordable, and famous  for its surprisingly great burgers.

name: Stonewall Inn
description: The birthplace of the modern gay rights movement. It functions beautifully as both a  living museum and a fiercely fun dive bar.

name: Bowery Ballroom
address: 6 Delancey St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: Arguably the best mid-sized live music venue in America. Impeccable acoustics, great  sightlines, and deep NYC indie history.
must_try: Catch an indie band before they blow up

name: Brooklyn Steel
description: A sprawling industrial venue retrofitted into a premier concert hall. It sounds incredible  and draws the biggest touring alternative acts.

name: Music Hall of Williamsburg
description: The quintessential Brooklyn rock club. Intimate enough to feel close to the stage, large  enough to attract serious talent.
must_try: Pre-show drinks in the basement lounge

name: Webster Hall
description: A massive, multi-tiered historic ballroom. Renovated but retaining its grit, it hosts  everyone from hip-hop legends to massive EDM raves.
must_try: Balcony view during a sold-out show

name: Blue Note Jazz Club
description: Legendary Greenwich Village jazz club. Two sets nightly featuring top-tier musicians. Intimate room, decent food, great cocktails.

name: Smalls Jazz Club
description: Basement jazz club that feels like a 1950s after-hours session. $20 cover, BYOB, no drink minimum. The real deal.

name: 230 Fifth
description: NYC's largest outdoor rooftop garden. It leans heavily tourist, but staring directly at the  Empire State Building from an outdoor igloo is undeniably fun.

name: Mr. Purple
address: 180 Orchard St 15th Floor, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: A pulsating, chaotic rooftop bar with a pool. It captures the modern, aggressive nightlife  spirit of the Lower East Side perfectly.

name: PHD Terrace
description: A glitzy midtown club masquerading as a terrace. Arrive early for the views, stay late if  you enjoy bottle service and loud music.

name: The Roof at PUBLIC
address: 215 Chrystie St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: Ian Schrager’s ultra-sleek, sexy penthouse lounge. The 360-degree views are  phenomenal, and the crowd is aggressively fashionable.

name: Compagnie des Vins Surnaturels
description: A sophisticated French wine bar that refuses to take itself too seriously. Play 'mystery  wine' with the sommelier to win a free bottle.

name: Ruffian
description: A wildly creative Eastern European-influenced wine bar. The orange wine selection is  exhaustive and the food defies categorization.

name: Wildair
address: 142 Orchard St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: The epicenter of NYC's natural wine movement. Tiny, cramped, and serving some of the  most inventive bar food in the city.

name: Bibble & Sip
description: An adorable Asian-French bakery famous for its massive cream puffs. A perfect  pre-theater sugar rush.

name: Breads Bakery
description: An Israeli-leaning bakery pumping out the best chocolate babka in the United States,  bar none.

name: Dominique Ansel Bakery
description: The birthplace of the Cronut. The line wraps down Spring Street, but the inventive,  rotating pastry menu justifies the hype.

name: Mah-Ze-Dahr Bakery
description: A sophisticated, jewel-box bakery. Everything is pristine, rich, and culturally diverse,  backed by Tom Colicchio.

name: Levain Bakery
address: 167 W 74th St, Upper West Side, Manhattan (+ multiple locations)
description: 6-ounce cookies that are basically a meal. The chocolate chip walnut is the one. Line forms early on weekends.

name: Devoción
description: Colombian single-origin coffee in a jaw-dropping greenhouse space. Beans go from farm to cup in ~10 days. One of the most beautiful cafes in the country.

name: Ample Hills Creamery
description: A beloved Brooklyn institution serving whimsical, mix-in heavy scoops. Perfect after a  walk through Prospect Park.
must_try: Ooey Gooey Butter Cake Ice Cream

name: Big Gay Ice Cream
description: What started as a food truck is now a legendary soft-serve empire. The concoctions are  salty, sweet, and wonderfully irreverent.

name: Morgenstern's Finest Ice Cream
address: 2 Rivington St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: A clinical, retro-chic parlor serving aggressively creative flavors. You've never had black  coconut ash ice cream before, but you need to.

name: Van Leeuwen Ice Cream
address: Multiple locations (original: 81 Bergen St, Boerum Hill, Brooklyn)
description: Started from a yellow truck, now a citywide empire. Honeycomb and Earl Grey flavors are cult favorites. Vegan options that actually taste good.

name: Black Fox Coffee
description: A multi-roaster cafe bringing absolute precision to FiDi. It is serious coffee for people  who obsess over extraction yields.

name: Partners Coffee
description: A bustling roastery in the heart of Williamsburg. You can watch the beans being roasted  while sipping a flawless flat white.

name: Sey Coffee
description: A light-drenched, plant-filled warehouse pouring the most meticulously sourced  light-roast coffee in North America.

name: Xi'an Famous Foods
description: Hand-pulled noodles and cumin lamb from western China. Spicy, salty, addictive. Multiple locations — find your closest one.
must_try: Spicy cumin lamb hand-ripped noodles (liang pi cold skin noodles too)

name: Ichiran
description: Solo dining booths designed to eliminate human interaction. The ultimate introvert  paradise serving intensely rich tonkotsu broth.

name: Ippudo
description: The spot that ignited NYC's modern ramen obsession. The energy is deafening and the  pork buns are legendary.
must_try: Akamaru Modern Ramen and Hirata Pork Buns

name: Jongro BBQ
description: Hidden on the second floor of K-Town, this spot mimics old-school Seoul. The meat  quality is elite and the atmosphere is wonderfully chaotic.

name: Nom Wah Tea Parlor
description: NYC's oldest dim sum parlor located on the infamous 'Bloody Angle'. Vintage diner  aesthetics meet made-to-order dumplings.
must_try: The Original Egg Roll and Roast Pork Bun

name: Pig and Khao
address: 68 Clinton St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: An unapologetic, hip-hop blasting Filipino-Thai mashup. The sizzle plates and  bottomless brunch are Lower East Side institutions.

name: Soothr
description: Michelin-recognized Thai comfort food in a hyper-stylized space. The cocktails are  potent and the noodle dishes pack serious heat.
must_try: Koong Karee (Shrimp Curry) and Duck Noodles

name: Sushi Nakazawa
description: High-end omakase born from the Jiro lineage. It is precise, theatrical, and demands  your full attention—and a hefty budget.

name: Sushi Yasuda
description: A purist sanctuary in Midtown. There are no spicy mayo rolls here; it is an exercise in  austere, perfect fish sourcing.

name: Tanoshi Sushi Sake Bar
address: 1372 York Ave, Upper East Side, Manhattan
description: A hidden, rustic omakase counter far east on the UES. It's strictly BYOB and offers  incredible value for the quality of fish.

name: Totto Ramen
description: A tiny, cash-only joint slinging incredible chicken-based paitan broth. You will leave  smelling like garlic and satisfaction.

name: Absolute Bagels
description: Thai-owned, cash-only perfection on the UWS. You will smell the malt from down the  block, and the crust-to-chew ratio is unmatched.
must_try: Hot Egg Bagel with Lox Spread

name: Ess-a-Bagel
description: These bagels are massive, doughy, and deeply satisfying. The line moves fast, but know  your order before you reach the counter.
must_try: Everything Bagel with Scallion Cream Cheese

name: Shelsky's Brooklyn Bagels
description: An authentic Brooklyn appetizing shop that refuses to compromise on tradition while  serving brilliant combinations like the 'Brooklyn Native'.
must_try: Sichuan Peppercorn Smoked Salmon on a Pumpernickel Bagel

name: Tompkins Square Bagels
description: A neighborhood anchor that treats bagel-making as serious craft. Expect outrageous  cream cheese flavors and a hipster crowd.
must_try: French Toast Bagel with Birthday Cake Cream Cheese

name: Dinosaur Bar-B-Que
description: An upstate legend that brought biker-bar energy to Harlem. Huge portions, loud blues  music, and highly dependable ribs.

name: Fette Sau
description: Dry-rubbed meats served by the pound in a converted auto-body shop. The whiskey list  is staggering and the communal tables are always packed.

name: Hometown Bar-B-Que
address: 454 Van Brunt St, Red Hook, Brooklyn
description: The undisputed king of NYC BBQ. Hidden deep in Red Hook, the lines are brutal but the  massive beef ribs and Caribbean-spiced meats justify the trek.

name: Mighty Quinn's Barbeque
description: The operation that taught Manhattan what real smoke tastes like. It is fast, casual, and  the burnt ends melt instantly.

name: Russ & Daughters
address: 179 E Houston St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: Appetizing shop since 1914. Lox, bagels, cream cheese, and smoked fish that defines what a New York breakfast is supposed to be.
must_try: Classic bagel with Nova Scotia lox and cream cheese

name: Balthazar
description: Keith McNally's Parisian brasserie in SoHo. The brunch is iconic. The steak frites at dinner is just as good. Still packed after 25+ years.

name: Clinton St. Baking Company
address: 4 Clinton St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: You will wait two hours on a sidewalk for these pancakes, and you won't regret a single  minute of it once the maple butter hits the table.

name: Cookshop
description: An absolute powerhouse for brunch near the High Line. Flawless farm-to-table eggs,  pastries, and bloody marys in a sun-drenched room.

name: Jack's Wife Freda
description: Mediterranean-American bistro that is essentially a SoHo fashion shoot come to life. The  green shakshuka is as beautiful as the crowd.

name: Sadelle's
description: A theatrical ode to New York appetizing culture. Waiters in waistcoats deliver  multi-tiered towers of bagels and lox in a stunning brick dining room.

name: Sunday in Brooklyn
description: A tri-level sanctuary of comfort food. The malted malt pancakes are ridiculously thick  and essentially double as dessert.

name: Di Fara Pizza
description: Legendary Brooklyn pizzeria. Every pie still made by hand, one at a time. The line is long and worth it.

name: Joe's Pizza
description: The default NYC slice. Thin, foldable, greasy in the right way. Cash only, eaten standing on the sidewalk, exactly as God intended.

name: Katz's Delicatessen
address: 205 E Houston St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: Open since 1888. The pastrami sandwich is a religious experience. Don't lose your ticket.
hours: Mon-Wed 8am-10:45pm, Thu 8am-2:45am, Fri 8am-24hrs, Sat 24hrs, Sun close 10:45pm

name: The Halal Guys
address: W 53rd St & 6th Ave (original cart), Midtown, Manhattan
description: The original street cart that launched an empire. Chicken and gyro over rice with white sauce and hot sauce. The line at 2am tells you everything.

name: Eleven Madison Park
description: Plant-based tasting menu from Daniel Humm in one of NYC's most stunning dining rooms. Controversial pivot, but the craft is undeniable.

name: Le Bernardin
description: Eric Ripert's three-Michelin-star seafood temple. The tasting menu is a masterclass. This is a bucket-list restaurant and it earns it.

name: Peter Luger Steak House
description: Cash-only Brooklyn steakhouse open since 1887. The porterhouse for two is the only thing on the menu that matters. No-frills service, world-class beef.

name: Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi
address: 10 Lincoln Center Plaza, Upper West Side, Manhattan
description: Afro-Caribbean fine dining at Lincoln Center from Kwame Onwuachi. One of the hardest reservations in the city. The suya-spiced duck is transcendent.

name: DeKalb Market Hall
address: 445 Albee Square W, Downtown Brooklyn, Brooklyn
description: A neon-lit subterranean maze of 40+ vendors. It hosts the only outer-borough outpost  of Katz's Deli and incredible Asian street food.

name: Time Out Market New York
description: A highly curated hall overlooking the East River. It compresses the best of NYC’s culinary  scene into one brick warehouse.
must_try: Clinton St. Baking Co. Pancakes or Bark Barbecue

name: Urbanspace Vanderbilt
description: A godsend for Midtown commuters and tourists alike. Fast, varied, and infinitely better  than the surrounding corporate chains.

name: Corner Bistro
description: One of the last real dives in the West Village. Paper plates, cheap McSorley's on tap, and  a towering, messy bacon cheeseburger.

name: JG Melon
description: A cash-only Upper East Side institution. It's cramped, covered in watermelon decor, and  serves an unpretentious, flawless pub burger.

name: Minetta Tavern
description: A Parisian steakhouse meets old-New York saloon. The Black Label Burger is a dry-aged  masterpiece that redefines the category.

name: Red Hook Tavern
address: 329 Van Brunt St, Red Hook, Brooklyn
description: An homage to classic NYC taverns. The dry-aged burger here is thick, perfectly crusted,  and demands ordering a serious bottle of wine.

name: L'Artusi
description: Modern Italian in the West Village that locals swear by. The spaghetti with crab is legendary. Bar seating is first-come-first-served and a great move.

name: Lucali
description: BYOB pizza joint in Carroll Gardens. Cash only, no slices — whole pies only. The crust is the best in the city, full stop. Line up before they open.
must_try: Margherita pizza with calzone on the side

name: Carbone
description: Red-sauce Italian amplified to an absurd, cinematic luxury. Securing a table is a  bloodsport, but the spicy rigatoni is genuinely flawless.

name: Don Angie
description: Modern Italian-American that commands legendary lines. The pinwheel lasagna for two  is visually stunning and functionally perfect.

name: I Sodi
description: A narrow, austere love letter to Tuscany. It has a cult following for its impossibly delicate,  multi-layered meat lasagna.

name: Lilia
description: Housed in a whitewashed former auto-body shop, Missy Robbins serves arguably the  best wood-fired seafood and pasta in Brooklyn.

name: Rezdôra
description: Emilia-Romagna regional pasta executed with Michelin-starred precision. The regional  pasta tasting menu is an absolute triumph.

name: Via Carota
description: The quintessential West Village gastroteca. The cacio e pepe is perfect and the garden  patio is the most charming outdoor dining in the Village.
must_try: Cacio e Pepe and Insalata Verde

name: Artichoke Basille's Pizza
description: Slices the size of hubcaps covered in thick, creamy artichoke dip. Best consumed after  five beers.

name: Mamoun's Falafel
description: The oldest falafel shop in NYC. It is a tiny, standing-room-only legend where the hot  sauce is genuinely dangerous.

name: Veselka
description: A Ukrainian diner holding down the East Village since 1954. Eating a bowl of borscht and  hand-crimped pierogi at 3 AM here is therapeutic.

name: Wo Hop
description: Located entirely in a basement, this is old-school Chinese-American comfort food. It's  loud, cheap, and a savior after midnight.

name: Los Tacos No. 1
description: Tiny stall inside Chelsea Market turning out perfect adobo chicken and carne asada tacos on fresh corn tortillas. The line moves fast.

name: Cervo's
address: 43 Canal St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: A narrow, natural-wine-fueled Iberian seafood joint. It is loud, unapologetically hip, and  serves some of the best shrimp heads in the city.
must_try: Crispy Shrimp Heads and Mussels Escabeche

name: Cobble Fish
address: 89 South St Pier 16, Seaport District, Manhattan
description: Casual, outdoor waterfront dining tucked between historic schooners. Feels more like a  nautical New England party than Manhattan.

name: Grand Central Oyster Bar
address: 89 E 42nd St (Grand Central Terminal), Midtown, Manhattan
description: An architectural and culinary institution. Sitting at the sweeping tiled counters with a  martini and local oysters is an NYC rite of passage.
must_try: Blue Point Oysters and Maryland Crab Cakes

name: Lobster Place
description: A chaotic, brilliant seafood counter inside Chelsea Market. Eat steamed lobster standing  up while navigating the tourist crowds.

name: Mar's
description: A glamorous, wood-paneled Astoria gem pulling Manhattanites to Queens for flawless  cocktails and pristine raw clams.

name: Oceans
description: Sleek and highly refined global seafood. It pulls a corporate crowd but the execution of  the raw bar is undeniably flawless.
must_try: Tuna Tartare and Lobster Mac and Cheese

name: Gallaghers Steakhouse
description: The only steakhouse in NYC still grilling over hickory coals. You can see the massive  dry-aging meat locker right from the sidewalk.

name: Keens Steakhouse
description: A living museum filled with tens of thousands of clay pipes. It is famously unpretentious  and serves a mutton chop that dwarfs standard steaks.

name: Quality Meats
description: A modern, industrial-chic take on the steakhouse format. The steak sauce is made  tableside and the bacon features peanut butter.

name: Barcade
description: The original arcade bar. Dozens of vintage 1980s arcade cabinets paired with an  aggressively curated local craft beer list.
must_try: Donkey Kong and a local IPA

name: Brooklyn Bowl
description: Bowling, fried chicken from Blue Ribbon, and live concerts. It is loud, messy, and the  perfect Williamsburg night out.
must_try: Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken while bowling

name: The Gutter
description: A dingy, beautiful retro bowling alley that refuses to modernize. It smells like cheap beer  and old wood, exactly as it should.
must_try: Pitcher of cheap beer and lane 1

name: Comedy Cellar
description: The most famous comedy club in the world. A-listers drop in unannounced to test new material. Book online and pray for a surprise guest.
must_try: Weekend late show (highest chance of drop-ins)

name: Madison Square Garden
description: The World's Most Famous Arena. Knicks, Rangers, concerts, boxing — the energy inside MSG on a big night is unmatched. Sits right on top of Penn Station.
must_try: Any Knicks home game for the atmosphere

name: Barclays Center
description: A rust-colored spaceship dropped in the middle of Brooklyn. Home to the Nets and  Liberty, boasting incredible sightlines and brutal ticket prices.

name: Citi Field
description: Home of the Mets. Arguably a better culinary experience than Yankee Stadium,  featuring Shake Shack and pastrami sandwiches.

name: Yankee Stadium
description: A monument to baseball imperialism. Take the D train up, grab a bucket of chicken, and  sit in the bleachers to hear the famous Roll Call.
must_try: Bleacher Creature Roll Call in the 1st inning

name: Arlo Hotels
description: Compact rooms, great rooftops, and design-forward vibes. The Williamsburg and NoMad locations are strongest. Solid mid-range pick.
must_try: Rooftop at Arlo NoMad at sunset

name: The Jane Hotel
description: Tiny cabin-style rooms in a stunning West Village building. Budget boutique in one of the best neighborhoods in the city. The ballroom bar is gorgeous.
must_try: The Ballroom lounge for a drink even if you're not a guest

name: Freehand New York
description: Boutique hostel energy with exceptional cocktail programs on the roof. Perfect for  younger travelers prioritizing vibe over square footage.

name: HI NYC Hostel
address: 891 Amsterdam Ave, Upper West Side, Manhattan
description: Clean, massive, and highly social. The biggest outdoor patio of any hostel in the city,  perfectly situated near Central Park.
must_try: Book a local walking tour at the desk

name: Moxy Times Square
description: Tiny, hyper-efficient rooms designed so you spend all your time in their sprawling  rooftop bar, Magic Hour.

name: Pod Hotels
address: Multiple locations (Pod 51: 230 E 51st St; Pod 39: 145 E 39th St; Pod Times Square)
description: Micro-hotel rooms with smart design. Not luxurious, but clean, well-located, and the rooftop bars are solid. Best budget option in Manhattan.

name: The Plaza Hotel
description: The most famous hotel in America. Overlooking Central Park and Grand Army Plaza since 1907. Even if you don't stay, walk through the lobby and have tea at the Palm Court.
must_try: Afternoon tea at The Palm Court

name: 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge
description: A stunning eco-luxury fortress right on the waterfront. The rooftop pool looking at the  financial district is absurdly beautiful.

name: Park Hyatt New York
description: Billionaire's Row opulence. The indoor pool plays classical music from Carnegie Hall  underwater through custom speakers.
must_try: Spa Nalai and the underwater music pool

name: The Mark Hotel
address: 25 E 77th St, Upper East Side, Manhattan
description: The epicenter of quiet Upper East Side luxury, famously where celebrities prepare for  the Met Gala. Jean-Georges handles the room service.

name: The Standard, High Line
description: Straddling the High Line, this hotel is a glass box of mid-century chic and uninhibited  voyeurism. The nightlife here is legendary.

name: EVEN Hotel Times Square South
description: A hotel explicitly focused on wellness. Rooms come with in-room fitness zones, TRX  bands, and standing desks.

name: Graduate Roosevelt Island
address: 22 N Loop Rd, Roosevelt Island, Manhattan
description: A bizarrely peaceful oasis accessed via aerial tram. The views of the East River and  Manhattan skyline from your bed are unbeatable.

name: The Hoxton, Williamsburg
description: British boutique cool imported to Brooklyn. The lobby is a permanent co-working space  for locals, and Laser Wolf on the roof is phenomenal.
must_try: Laser Wolf Israeli Skewers on the roof

name: citizenM New York Times Square
description: Micro-rooms controlled entirely by an iPad. What it lacks in space, it makes up for with a  stunning lobby and rooftop bar.

name: The Collective Paper Factory
description: A repurposed 100-year-old paper factory in Queens. It offers massive spaces, industrial  chic, and quick subway access to Manhattan.

name: Wythe Hotel
description: The pioneer of Brooklyn boutique hotels in a converted factory. Exposed brick, massive  windows, and incredible Manhattan views.

name: Brighton Beach
description: Just down the boardwalk from Coney Island, offering a slightly quieter stretch of sand  backed by incredible Eastern European groceries and cafes.
must_try: Vodka and pelmeni on the boardwalk

name: Coney Island
description: An unapologetically kitschy, historic boardwalk. Come for the hot dogs, the rickedy  Cyclone roller coaster, and prime people-watching.
must_try: Nathan's Famous Hot Dog and The Cyclone

name: Brooklyn Bridge Park Greenway
address: Pier 1 to Pier 6, DUMBO/Brooklyn Heights, Brooklyn
description: The most picturesque bike path in America. You ride directly under the bridges with the  lower Manhattan skyline looming across the water.
must_try: Sunset ride from DUMBO to Red Hook

name: Central Park Loop
description: A 6-mile, car-free circuit. It's the most efficient way to see the park, but watch out for  the aggressive Lycra-clad cyclists.
must_try: Riding through the tree canopy in the northern end

name: Citi Bike
description: The fastest way to traverse Manhattan avenues. The e-bikes flatten hills and make  conquering the bridges thrilling rather than exhausting.

name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
description: 52 acres of curated gardens. The Japanese Hill-and-Pond Garden is the jewel. Cherry blossom season (late April) is absolutely mobbed — go early on a weekday.
must_try: Cherry Blossom Festival (Hanami) in late April/early May

name: Brooklyn Bridge
description: Walk from Manhattan to Brooklyn (or the other way). Go early morning or at sunset to avoid the crowds. End in DUMBO for the best skyline photo in the city.
must_try: Walk Brooklyn→Manhattan at sunset, or Manhattan→Brooklyn and grab pizza at Juliana's

name: Central Park
description: 843 acres of green in the middle of Manhattan. Bethesda Fountain, the Ramble, Strawberry Fields, the Reservoir — each section is its own world. Free Shakespeare in the Park in summer.
must_try: Row a boat at the Loeb Boathouse (or Bow Bridge at sunset)

name: Governors Island
address: Governors Island, New York Harbor (ferry from Battery Maritime Building or Pier 6 Brooklyn)
description: 172-acre island in the harbor with hills, hammocks, art installations, and the best skyline views without paying for an observation deck. Free ferries on weekends before noon.
must_try: The Hills (climb Outlook Hill for panoramic views)

name: The High Line
address: Gansevoort St to 34th St, West Side, Manhattan
description: Elevated park on a former rail line running 1.45 miles along the west side. Public art, native plantings, and views of the Hudson. Start at the Gansevoort end near the Whitney.
must_try: Walk north to south at sunset for Hudson River views

name: Downtown Boathouse
address: Pier 26 at N Moore St, Tribeca, Manhattan
description: Entirely volunteer-run, free kayaking on the Hudson. A bizarre and peaceful  juxtaposition against the towering skyscrapers behind you.

name: Manhattan Kayak
description: Guided kayak and SUP tours on the Hudson. Feeling the current of the river while  staring at skyscrapers is uniquely exhilarating.

name: Staten Island Ferry
description: The best free tour in New York. You get massive views of the Statue of Liberty and the  harbor without paying a dime.
must_try: Grab a cheap beer from the concession and stand on the outer deck

name: NYC Ferry
address: Multiple stops across all five boroughs
description: Six routes connecting Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Staten Island. $4 per ride, incredible skyline views. The commute that feels like a cruise.
must_try: Rockaway route for beach access or Soundview route for Bronx waterfront

name: Trader Joe's Wine Shop
description: The cheapest decent wine in Manhattan. Separate from the grocery store (NYC law). The $3.99 bottles are legitimately fine.
must_try: Stock up before a BYOB dinner (Lucali, Smalls)

name: Whole Foods Market
description: A massive subterranean grocery store perfect for grabbing a high-quality picnic before  heading directly into Central Park.
must_try: The hot food bar for a park picnic

name: Zabar's
description: An Upper West Side chaotic masterpiece. You come here to dodge aggressive  grandmothers and buy the best smoked fish and coffee beans in town.
must_try: Nova Lox and Zabar's Blend Coffee

name: LuggageHero Columbus Circle
address: Local shops near 59th St, Columbus Circle, Manhattan
description: An essential app-based network of local bodegas and shops that hold your bags safely  after you check out of your hotel.

name: Duane Reade (Times Square)
description: The quintessential NYC convenience store. When you need blister pads, an umbrella,  and cheap water at 2 AM, this is where you go.

name: CityMD
description: Walk-in urgent care on practically every other block in Manhattan. No appointment needed. The NYC answer to 'I need a doctor now.'

name: Brooklyn Flea
address: 80 Pearl St, DUMBO, Brooklyn (+ seasonal locations)
description: Vintage furniture, clothing, records, and crafts from 150+ vendors. The DUMBO location has Manhattan skyline views between the finds.
must_try: Vintage leather jackets + skyline photos from the waterfront

name: Books Are Magic
description: Owned by author Emma Straub, this is Brooklyn's coziest, most community-driven  bookshop. Very high chance of spotting local authors.

name: McNally Jackson
description: A sophisticated, beautifully curated independent bookstore. The literature sections are  arranged by nation of origin.

name: Fifth Avenue Shopping
description: Saks, Bergdorf Goodman, Tiffany & Co., Louis Vuitton — the most famous shopping strip on Earth. Even window shopping is an experience.

name: SoHo Shopping District
address: SoHo (Houston to Canal, Broadway to 6th Ave), Manhattan
description: Cast-iron architecture lined with flagship stores, independent boutiques, and gallery-adjacent shops. The cobblestone streets are the backdrop.
must_try: Walk Prince St and Mercer St for the best mix of indie and luxury

name: Chelsea Market
description: Indoor market in a former Nabisco factory. Food stalls, independent shops, and the entrance to the High Line. Lobster Place for seafood, Artists & Fleas for vintage.
must_try: Los Tacos No. 1 + Doughnuttery mini donuts

name: Smorgasburg
address: Williamsburg (Sat) / Prospect Park (Sun), Brooklyn (locations vary seasonally)
description: Outdoor food market with 100+ vendors. Where NYC food trends are born. The raindrop cake started here. Go hungry.
seasonal: Outdoor season April-October, indoor winter market

name: A1 Records
description: A digger's paradise. Stacks of used hip-hop, soul, and jazz vinyl. It requires patience, but  the finds are unparalleled.

name: Academy Records
description: The best spot in the city for classical, jazz, and rock CDs and LPs. Quiet, extremely  organized, and reasonably priced.

name: Rough Trade NYC
description: The UK indie giant relocated to Rockefeller Center. It feels corporate on the outside, but  the vinyl selection remains impeccably curated.

name: Brooklyn Industries
description: The quintessential Brooklyn streetwear brand. Better souvenirs than anything you'll find  in Times Square.

name: Eataly NYC Flatiron
description: An overwhelming, multi-level Italian food emporium. Grab a glass of Barolo and wander  through aisles of imported prosciutto and fresh pasta.
must_try: Fresh pasta counter and rooftop dining

name: Economy Candy
address: 108 Rivington St, Lower East Side, Manhattan
description: A floor-to-ceiling sugar rush operating since 1937. A glorious, chaotic mess of nostalgia  and bulk chocolate.

name: Russian & Turkish Baths
description: An unapologetic, gritty East Village institution since 1892. Do not expect luxury; expect  intense heat, eucalyptus, and a bizarrely loyal clientele.

name: Aire Ancient Baths
description: Roman-style thermal baths in a restored Tribeca warehouse. Candlelit pools at different temperatures. Feels like you left the city entirely.
must_try: Thermal bath experience + wine bath upgrade

name: The Spa at Mandarin Oriental
description: Floor-to-ceiling Central Park views from the treatment rooms 35 floors up. The Oriental Essence massage is the signature. This is the splurge spa.
must_try: Oriental Essence massage with Central Park views

name: Sky Ting Yoga
description: A bright, airy studio favoring a relaxed, unpretentious approach to yoga. You will leave  feeling stretched, calm, and incredibly hip.

name: TMPL Gym
description: A luxury, neon-lit fitness club that feels like a nightclub. The saltwater pool and  immersive spin classes are top-tier.

name: Y7 Studio
address: 250 E Houston St, East Village, Manhattan
description: Sweat-drenched, candlelit vinyasa yoga set to heavy hip-hop. It is dark, intense, and  aggressively modern.
